title.narrative: Strengthening Public Financial Management Program, Subprogram 1

description.narrative: The programmatic approach seeks to increase the availability and efficiency of public services in Cambodia, including services for poor and vulnerable groups, by strengthening public expenditure and revenue management. In support of stage 3 of the government's four-stage Public Financial Management Reform Program (PFMRP), the proposed program will finance actions and initiatives to strengthen (i) the policy and regulatory framework for expenditure and revenue management, (ii) the procedures and capacities of select line ministries to implement budgeting and expenditure management reforms, and (iii) the capacity of the external audit function. The proposed program is included in the country operations business plan, 2016-2018 for Cambodia of the Asian Development Bank (ADB).

Output: Capacity of selected line ministries to implement budgeting and expenditure management reforms improved. Indicator: Annual financial and performance reports prepared and published by at least six line ministries (2015 baseline: 0). (Subprogram 2 and TA Loan ) Progress/Status: All six ministries produce monthly, quarterly and annual financial and performance reports for MEF based on program budget structures. These reports are not yet produced in a user-friendly format for the public and only two of the six ministries publish reports on ministry websites. Further work is needed to improve reporting formats and the reports to be published on the websites of the ministries. Data Source: MEF and line ministry annual progress reports. Actual value:

Output: Capacity of selected line ministries to implement budgeting and expenditure management reforms improved. Indicator: FMIS implementation plans, including business process and change-management strategies, prepared by at least 6 line ministries under phase 2 of FMIS (2015 baseline: 0). (Subprogram 2 and TA Loan ) Progress/Status: Three of the six ministries are not in the first batch for phase 2 of FMIS implementation and they have not yet commenced preparatory work, awaiting further advice from MEF. Three ministries are in the first batch for implementation (MOEYS, MAFF and MOLVT), and they have undertaken initial business process reviews and established working groups for planning the implementation, including on business process re-engineering and change management. All six line ministries are expected to have implementation plans by early 2019. Data Source: MEF and line ministry annual progress reports. Actual value:

Output: Capacity of selected line ministries to implement budgeting and expenditure management reforms improved. Indicator: Financial management manuals for budget preparation, execution, and financial and performance reporting prepared in at least six ministries (2015 baseline: 0). (Subprogram 2 and TA Loan ) Progress/Status: While rudimentary manuals based on consolidation of past MEF guidelines and instructions are in place in the six ministries, these are not yet comprehensive and in user friendly formats. It is suggested that MEF issue instructions to line ministries to prepare customized financial manuals based on a comprehensive financial management manual to be issued by MEF by the second quarter 2018. Data Source: MEF and line ministry annual progress reports. Actual value:

Output: Capacity of selected line ministries to implement budgeting and expenditure management reforms improved. Indicator: Performance audits and audits of ICT included in internal audit plans and implemented in at least six ministries (2015 baseline: 0). (Subprogram 2 and TA Loan ) Progress/Status: Most internal audit departments have not undertaken major performance based audits although three of the six departments have undertaken some preliminary ones. None of the six ministries have yet undertaken any substantial work on ICT audits. Data Source: MEF and line ministry annual progress reports. Actual value:

Output: Capacity of selected line ministries to implement budgeting and expenditure management reforms improved. Indicator: Program budgeting with integrated capital and recurrent budgets fully implemented and issues of gender and poverty included by at least six ministries (2015 baseline: 0). (Subprogram 2 and TA Loan ) Progress/Status: All six ministries are producing program budgets with some coverage of poverty in policy frameworks and objectives and, in most cases, some activities for poverty and gender specifically funded. Rudimentary commencement of integrating capital and recurrent budgets (mainly for the government funded budget only) has commenced in four of the six ministries but further work is needed for each ministry to integrate current and capital budgets based on more detailed guidelines for integration being developed by MEF. Program budgets for 2018 and 2019 will be reviewed in early 2019. Data Source: MEF and line ministry annual progress reports. Actual value:

Output: Capacity of the external audit function improved. Output: Policy and regulatory framework for expenditure and revenue management strengthened. Indicator: MTRMS implemented with revenues (excluding grants) growing over the medium term on average at 0.5 percentage point of GDP a year—or from a total of 13.5% of GDP in FY2013 to 16.0% of GDP in FY2018 (2013 baseline: 13.5% of GDP). (Subprogram 2 and TA Loan) Progress/Status: Targets of 0.5% per annum have been significantly exceeded for 2015 and 2016 and end period target of 16.0% of GDP has already been exceeded. Data Source: MEF annual progress reports. Actual value:

Output: Capacity of selected line ministries to implement budgeting and expenditure management reforms improved. Indicator: BSPs annually updated and annual program budgeting prepared with poverty and gender issues included by at least six line ministries (2015 baseline: 3). (Subprogram 2 and TA Loan ) Progress/Status: All six ministries are producing BSPs with some coverage of poverty in policy frameworks and objectives and, in most cases, some activities for gender and poverty reduction specifically funded. The term of reference of the international public sector planning and budget specialist has been revised to include a comprehensive review of budget strategic plan formats and procedures for the six ministries in addition to further strengthening and comprehensive coverage of poverty and gender matters. The BSPs for 2018 and 2019 will be further reviewed in early 2019. Data Source: MEF and line ministry annual progress reports. Actual value:
